        layer_indices = list(range(model_config.num_hidden_layers))
    else:
        layer_indices = [int(l) for l in args.layers.split(",")]

    # Run name
    model_short = args.model.split("/")[-1]
    if args.run_name is None:
        # Include position so prefill/last/all sweeps with otherwise identical
        # hyperparams don't collide on disk (same bug as train_rl.py had).
        pos_suffix = f"_pos{args.position}" if args.mode != "lora" else ""
        args.run_name = (
            f"{model_short}_sft_{args.mode}"
            f"_r{args.rank}_lr{args.lr:.0e}{pos_suffix}"
        )

    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"SFT Training: {args.run_name}")
    print(f"  Model: {args.model}")
    print(f"  Rank: {args.rank}, Layers: {len(layer_indices)}, Position: {args.position}")
    print(f"  LR: {args.lr}, Epochs: {args.epochs}")
    print(f"{'='*60}\n")

    # Load tokenizer
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = [REDACTED]
    # Base Llama models ship with chat_template=None. Use a SIMPLE template
    # that adds no special tokens — just `User:`/`Assistant:` labels around
    # bos/eos. Lets us probe whether the base can learn instruction-following
    # cheaply without piggybacking on the Llama-3 Instruct format.
    if tokenizer.chat_template is None:
        tokenizer.chat_template = (
            "{{ bos_token }}"
            "{% for m in messages %}"
            "{% if m['role'] == 'user' %}User: {{ m['content'] }}\n"
            "{% elif m['role'] == 'assistant' %}Assistant: {{ m['content'] }}{{ eos_token }}"
            "{% elif m['role'] == 'system' %}{{ m['content'] }}\n"
            "{% endif %}"
            "{% endfor %}"
            "{% if add_generation_prompt %}Assistant: {% endif %}"
        )
        print(f"  chat_template set to simple User:/Assistant: format")

    # Load and preprocess dataset
    # Strategy: always derive eval from a fixed 50k base pool so eval sets are
    # identical across runs with different max_n_train_example.
    #   1. Shuffle full dataset, take first 50k/(1-eval_split) as base pool
    #   2. Split base pool into train_base (50k) + eval using train_test_split
    #   3. If max_n_train_example > 50k, append extra examples from the remainder
    # This ensures eval is always the same regardless of training set size.
    print(f"Loading {args.dataset}...")
    ds_config = args.dataset_config
    if ds_config is None and "gsm8k" in args.dataset.lower():
        ds_config = "main"

    # Datasets that ship with their own train/test split — match train_rl.py
    # and use the built-in test split as eval rather than re-splitting train.
    is_gsm8k = "gsm8k" in args.dataset.lower()
    is_math = "hendrycks_math" in args.dataset.lower()
    has_builtin_test = is_gsm8k or is_math

    def _load(split):
        # MATH special-case: hendrycks_math is published as 7 subject configs
        # rather than one. Concat them all to match rl_training/data.py:36-41.
        if is_math:
            from datasets import concatenate_datasets
            subjects = [
                "algebra", "counting_and_probability", "geometry",
                "intermediate_algebra", "number_theory", "prealgebra", "precalculus",
            ]
            parts = [load_dataset(args.dataset, s, split=split) for s in subjects]
            return concatenate_datasets(parts)
        if ds_config is not None:
            return load_dataset(args.dataset, ds_config, split=split)
        return load_dataset(args.dataset, split=split)

    if has_builtin_test:
        raw_train = _load("train").shuffle(seed=args.seed)
        raw_eval = _load("test")
        if args.max_n_train_example and args.max_n_train_example < len(raw_train):
            raw_train = raw_train.select(range(args.max_n_train_example))
    else:
        raw_dataset = _load("train").shuffle(seed=args.seed)

        base_n_train = 50000
        base_pool_size = int(base_n_train / (1 - args.eval_split))
        base_pool_size = min(base_pool_size, len(raw_dataset))
        base_pool = raw_dataset.select(range(base_pool_size))

        base_split = base_pool.train_test_split(test_size=args.eval_split, seed=args.seed)
        raw_eval = base_split["test"]
        raw_train = base_split["train"]

        # max_n_train_example > base pool: pull extra examples from the remainder.
        # max_n_train_example <= base pool: truncate (the previous code path
        # silently used the full base pool, which made smoketest configs do real
        # sweep-sized runs).
        if args.max_n_train_example and args.max_n_train_example > len(raw_train):
            extra_needed = args.max_n_train_example - len(raw_train)
            extra_start = base_pool_size
            extra_end = min(extra_start + extra_needed, len(raw_dataset))
            if extra_end > extra_start:
                from datasets import concatenate_datasets
                extra = raw_dataset.select(range(extra_start, extra_end))
                raw_train = concatenate_datasets([raw_train, extra])
        elif args.max_n_train_example and args.max_n_train_example < len(raw_train):
            raw_train = raw_train.select(range(args.max_n_train_example))

    # Multi-rank: only rank 0 runs the .map() (which writes per-shard arrow
    # cache files); other ranks wait on a barrier and then memory-map the
    # finished cache.  Without this, concurrent num_proc=8 workers across
    # ranks race on the same cache directory and crash with FileNotFoundError
    # on .arrow files that haven't been atomically renamed yet.
    with state.main_process_first():
        dataset = preprocess_chat(raw_train, tokenizer, max_length=args.max_length, position=args.position)
        train_dataset = dataset
        eval_dataset = preprocess_chat(raw_eval, tokenizer, max_length=args.max_length, position=args.position)
    if args.max_eval_samples and len(eval_dataset) > args.max_eval_samples:
        eval_dataset = eval_dataset.select(range(args.max_eval_samples))
    print(f"Train: {len(train_dataset)}, Eval: {len(eval_dataset)}")

    # Load model
    print(f"Loading model: {args.model}")
    attn_impl = "flash_attention_2" if args.use_flash_attn else None
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model,
        torch_dtype=torch_dtype,
        attn_implementation=attn_impl,
    )
    # Activation checkpointing (HF gradient_checkpointing OR FSDP's
    # fsdp_activation_checkpointing) reuses the same Cache object across
    # forward and recompute. With use_cache=True, recompute would call
    # past_key_values.update() a second time and the returned K/V doubles
    # in the seq dim — surfaces as torch.utils.checkpoint.CheckpointError
    # ("Recomputed values ... have different metadata"). HF's LlamaModel
    # auto-disables use_cache when self.gradient_checkpointing is True,
    # but FSDP-side activation checkpointing doesn't set that flag, so
    # the auto-disable never fires. Always off for training.
    model.config.use_cache = False

    # MoE: with the base frozen, the router load-balance loss only adds
    # noise to adapter gradients (frozen routers can't learn from it).
    # Silent no-op for dense models.
    if hasattr(model.config, "router_aux_loss_coef"):
        model.config.router_aux_loss_coef = 0.0
        if hasattr(model.config, "output_router_logits"):
            model.config.output_router_logits = False
        print("  MoE detected: router_aux_loss_coef -> 0.0, output_router_logits -> False")

    # Apply adapter
    if args.mode in ("lora", "dora", "rslora", "vera"):
        if not PEFT_AVAILABLE:
            raise RuntimeError("peft required for LoRA/DoRA/VeRA. Install with: pip install peft")
        for param in model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
        # PEFT + gradient_checkpointing needs input embeddings to require grad,
        # otherwise backward raises "element 0 does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn".
        if args.gradient_checkpointing and hasattr(model, "enable_input_require_grads"):
            model.enable_input_require_grads()

        if args.mode == "vera":
            from peft import VeraConfig
            peft_config = VeraConfig(
                r=args.rank,
                target_modules=args.lora_modules.split(","),
                vera_dropout=0.05,
                bias="none",
                task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
            )
        else:
            peft_config = LoraConfig(
                r=args.rank,
                lora_alpha=args.lora_alpha,
                target_modules=args.lora_modules.split(","),
                lora_dropout=0.0,
                bias="none",
                task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
                use_dora=(args.mode == "dora"),
                use_rslora=(args.mode == "rslora"),
            )
        model = get_peft_model(model, peft_config)
        model.print_trainable_parameters()
        if args.gradient_checkpointing:
            # Required when the base model is frozen under PEFT: forces input
            # embeddings to require grad so checkpointed blocks have a grad path.
            model.enable_input_require_grads()
    else:
        # LoReFT / other intervention adapters
        
        from dataclasses import fields as _dc_fields
        _preft_fields = {f.name for f in _dc_fields(PreftConfig)}
        _preft_kwargs = dict(
            layer_indices=layer_indices,
            adapter_type=args.mode,
            low_rank_dim=args.rank,
            position=args.position,
            frozen=False,
            use_residual=True,
            logging=args.reft_logging,
        )
        preft_config = PreftConfig(**_preft_kwargs)
        model = get_preft_model(model, preft_config)
        if args.gradient_checkpointing and hasattr(model, "enable_input_require_grads"):
            # Same fix as the PEFT branch: if the base model has all-frozen
            # params, the first checkpointed segment has no grad-path. Safe to
            # call unconditionally when supported.
            model.enable_input_require_grads()

    trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    total = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    print(f"Trainable params: {trainable:,} / {total:,} ({100 * trainable / total:.4f}%)")

    # Output dir
    output_dir = os.path.join(args.output_dir, args.run_name)

    # Training args
    training_args = TrainingArguments(
        output_dir=output_dir,
        num_train_epochs=args.epochs,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=args.eval_batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=args.gradient_accumulation_steps,
        learning_rate=args.lr,
        lr_scheduler_type=args.schedule,
        warmup_ratio=args.warmup_ratio,
        weight_decay=args.weight_decay,
        logging_steps=10,
        eval_strategy="steps",
        eval_steps=args.eval_steps,
        save_strategy="no" if "shared" in args.mode else "steps",
        save_steps=args.eval_steps,
        save_total_limit=2,
        save_only_model=True,
        report_to="wandb" if args.use_wandb else "none",
        run_name=args.run_name,
        seed=args.seed,
        bf16=(args.dtype == "bfloat16"),
        fp16=(args.dtype == "float16"),
        remove_unused_columns=False,
        dataloader_num_workers=4,
        gradient_checkpointing=args.gradient_checkpointing,
        gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False} if args.gradient_checkpointing else None,
        # Note: prediction_loss_only=True is omitted — combined with
        # compute_metrics=None on recent transformers it suppresses the
        # eval_loss key from the metrics dict, leaving only eval_runtime/spp
        # in the log.  Default (False) is fine; we still don't aggregate
        # logits because compute_metrics is None.
        label_names=["labels"],  # PreftModel.forward has no explicit `labels` kwarg;
                                  # without this Trainer.find_labels returns [] and eval skips loss.
        use_liger_kernel=args.use_liger_kernel,
        # HF Trainer auto-detection only turns this off when the model is a
        # PreTrainedModel; PreftModel falls through to True, which makes DDP
        # walk the autograd graph every backward step for no reason (ReFT
        # never has unused params — every adapter fires on every forward).
        ddp_find_unused_parameters=False,
    )

    # wandb init
    if args.use_wandb:
        wandb.init(
            entity=ENTITY,
            project=args.wandb_project,
            name=args.run_name,
            config={
                **vars(args),
                "layer_indices": layer_indices,
                "trainable_params": trainable,
                "total_params": total,
            },
        )

    # Data collator
    data_collator = DataCollatorForSeq2Seq(
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        padding=True,
        return_tensors="pt",
    )

    # Trainer
    trainer_cls = Trainer if args.mode in ("lora", "dora", "rslora", "vera") else SFTTrainerWithSave
    trainer = trainer_cls(
        model=model,
        args=training_args,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        eval_dataset=eval_dataset,
        data_collator=data_collator,
    )

    # Debug: show intervention positions for first example (ReFT only)
    if args.mode not in ("lora", "dora", "rslora", "vera"):
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"Intervention debug (position={args.position})")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        debug_example = train_dataset[0]
        tokens = debug_example["input_ids"]
        labels = debug_example["labels"]
        loc = debug_example["intervention_locations"]
        seq_len = len(tokens)
        print(f"Total tokens: {seq_len}, Intervention location: {loc}")

        # Position semantics (matches BaseAdapter._apply_delta):
        #   "all"      → every position
        #   "prefill"  → positions 0..loc inclusive (whole prompt)
        #   "last"     → only loc
        #   "first"    → only loc (==0 by construction)
        def _is_intervened(i):
            if args.position == "all":
                return True
            if args.position == "prefill":
                return i <= loc
            return i == loc

        window = 5
        start = max(0, loc - window)
        end = min(seq_len, loc + window + 1)
        n_intervened = (
            seq_len if args.position == "all" else
            (loc + 1) if args.position == "prefill" else 1
        )
        print(f"Total tokens: {seq_len}, anchor loc: {loc}, "
              f"intervened positions: {n_intervened}")
        for i in range(start, end):
            tok_str = tokenizer.decode([tokens[i]])
            role = "PROMPT" if labels[i] == IGNORE_INDEX else "COMPL"
            marker = " <<< INTERVENED" if _is_intervened(i) else ""
            print(f"  [{i:4d}] {role:6s} {tok_str!r}{marker}")
        print(f"{'='*60}\n")

    # Train (eval happens automatically via eval_strategy="steps")
    import transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama as _llama_mod
    print(f"[liger check] LlamaForCausalLM.forward = {_llama_mod.LlamaForCausalLM.forward.__qualname__}")
    print(f"[liger check] use_liger_kernel = {training_args.use_liger_kernel}")
    print("\nStarting training...")
    trainer.train()

    # Save via Trainer so FSDP runs go through SFTTrainerWithSave's
    # _save_preft_adapters_fsdp (gathers params on rank 0 + rank-guards the
    # write).  A direct model.save_pretrained() from all ranks races on
    # the same path and produces unloadable files; checkpoint saves via
    # trainer.save_model() do not have that problem.
    print(f"\nSaving to {output_dir}")
    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    trainer.save_model(output_dir)
    if trainer.args.process_index == 0:
        tokenizer.save_pretrained(output_dir)
        with open(os.path.join(output_dir, "training_args.json"), "w") as f:
            json.dump({**vars(args), "layer_indices": layer_indices}, f, indent=2)

    if args.use_wandb:
        wandb.finish()

    print("Done!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Evaluate a trained ReFT or LoRA checkpoint on the GSM8K test set.

Uses vLLM for fast batched generation when available, falls back to
HuggingFace model.generate() otherwise.

Usage:
    # Single checkpoint
    uv run python eval.py --checkpoint ./outputs/run_name

    # All checkpoints under outputs/
    uv run python eval.py --sweep_dir ./outputs

    # Force HF backend (no vLLM)
    uv run python eval.py --checkpoint ./outputs/run_name --backend hf
"""

except ImportError:

# Llama-3 has two EOS variants (`<|end_of_text|>`, `<|eot_id|>`); chat-tuned
# SFT emits the latter but `tokenizer.eos_token_id` often returns only the
# former. Qwen has `<|im_end|>`. Collect all of them so vLLM actually stops.
_EOS_TOKEN_CANDIDATES = ("<|eot_id|>", "<|end_of_text|>", "<|im_end|>")


def _collect_stop_ids(tokenizer) -> list[int]:
    ids: list[int] = []
    if tokenizer.eos_token_id is not None:
        ids.append(tokenizer.eos_token_id)
    unk = getattr(tokenizer, "unk_token_id", None)
    for tok in _EOS_TOKEN_CANDIDATES:
        tid = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tok)
        if isinstance(tid, int) and tid != unk and tid not in ids:
            ids.append(tid)
    return ids

def _get_base_model_name(checkpoint_dir: Path) -> str:
    candidate_files = (
        ("preft_config.json", ("base_model_name_or_path",)),
        ("reft_config.json", ("base_model_name_or_path",)),
        ("tokenizer_config.json", ("name_or_path", "_name_or_path")),
        ("training_config.json", ("model_name", "model_name_or_path")),
        ("adapter_config.json", ("base_model_name_or_path",)),
        ("config.json", ("_name_or_path", "name_or_path")),
    )
    for filename, keys in candidate_files:
        path = checkpoint_dir / filename
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            payload = json.load(f)
        for key in keys:
            value = payload.get(key)
            if isinstance(value, str) and value:
                return value
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Could not resolve base model name for checkpoint {checkpoint_dir}. "
        f"Looked for a non-empty string in: "
        f"preft_config.json:base_model_name_or_path, "
        f"tokenizer_config.json:(_)name_or_path, "
        f"training_config.json:model_name(_or_path), "
        f"adapter_config.json:base_model_name_or_path, "
        f"config.json:(_)name_or_path. "
        f"Write the base model into one of these fields (e.g. add "
        f"`base_model_name_or_path` to preft_config.json) and re-run."
    )


def _resolve_reft_weights_path(checkpoint_dir: Path) -> Path:
    candidates = (
        "loreft_weights.safetensors",
        "reft_weights.safetensors",
        "intervention_weights.safetensors",
        "adapter_model.safetensors",
    )
    for name in candidates:
        path = checkpoint_dir / name
        if path.exists():
            return path
    return checkpoint_dir / "loreft_weights.safetensors"


def _detect_checkpoint_type(checkpoint_dir: Path) -> str:
    """Return 'lora', 'reft', or raise."""
    if (checkpoint_dir / "adapter_config.json").exists():
        return "lora"
    if (checkpoint_dir / "preft_config.json").exists():
        return "reft"
    if (checkpoint_dir / "reft_config.json").exists():
        return "reft"
    if (checkpoint_dir / "intervention_config.json").exists():
        return "reft"
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"No adapter config found in {checkpoint_dir}")


def _detect_training_type(checkpoint_dir: Path) -> str:
    """Return 'sft', 'rl', or 'unknown'.

    SFT runs (train_sft.py:675) write training_args.json. RL runs
    (train_rl.py:329) write training_config.json. Either file existing
    means training finished — useful as a dedup marker too.
    """
    if (checkpoint_dir / "training_args.json").exists():
        return "sft"
    if (checkpoint_dir / "training_config.json").exists():
        return "rl"
    return "unknown"

def _load_tokenizer(checkpoint_dir: Path, model_name: str):
    if normalize_checkpoint_tokenizer_config(checkpoint_dir):
        print("  Normalized tokenizer_config.json for current Transformers compatibility.")
    tokenizer = load_checkpoint_tokenizer(checkpoint_dir, fallback_model_name=model_name)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = [REDACTED]
    tokenizer.padding_side = "left"
    # SFT runs that train on raw-text formats (e.g. GSM8K's "Question:/Answer:")
    # save a tokenizer_config.json without chat_template. Cross-task evals that
    # need apply_chat_template then fail — pull the template from the base
    # model as a fallback. Chat template is pure formatting, so this doesn't
    # affect trained weights.
    if not getattr(tokenizer, "chat_template", None):
        try:
            from transformers import AutoTokenizer

            base_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
            if getattr(base_tok, "chat_template", None):
                tokenizer.chat_template = base_tok.chat_template
                print(f"  Borrowed chat_template from base model: {model_name}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  Could not load base tokenizer to borrow chat_template: {e}")
    return tokenizer

#  vLLM backend                                                        #

def _load_reft_vllm(checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer, num_gpus, gpu_mem, enforce_eager):
    weights_path = _resolve_reft_weights_path(checkpoint_dir)
    if not weights_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"ReFT weights not found in {checkpoint_dir}")

    tokenizer_source = resolve_tokenizer_source(checkpoint_dir, model_name)

    llm_kwargs = {
        "tokenizer": str(tokenizer_source),
        "trust_remote_code": True,
        "tensor_parallel_size": max(1, num_gpus),
        "gpu_memory_utilization": gpu_mem,
        "enable_prefix_caching": False,
    }
    if enforce_eager:
        llm_kwargs["enforce_eager"] = True
        llm_kwargs["compilation_config"] = {"level": 0}

    try:
        llm = PreftModel.build_vllm_from_checkpoint(
            checkpoint_dir, model_name, **llm_kwargs)
    except Exception as exc:
        if enforce_eager:
            raise
        print(f"  vLLM graph mode failed ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc}). Retrying eager.")
        gc.collect()
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        llm_kwargs["enforce_eager"] = True
        llm_kwargs["compilation_config"] = {"level": 0}
        llm = PreftModel.build_vllm_from_checkpoint(
            checkpoint_dir, model_name, **llm_kwargs)

    return {"backend": "vllm", "llm": llm, "tokenizer": tokenizer}


def _detect_lora_position(checkpoint_dir):
    """Recover the LoRA gating position the checkpoint was trained with.

    Returns the value to pass as LoRARequest(lora_position=...), or None for
    a vanilla full-position LoRA. Sources, in order:
      * training_config.json["lora_position"]   — RL trainer
      * training_args.json["position"]          — SFT prefill-only LoRA
      * prefill_only_lora.json present          — SFT marker fallback
    """
    cfg_path = checkpoint_dir / "training_config.json"
    if cfg_path.exists():
        with open(cfg_path) as f:
            value = json.load(f).get("lora_position")
        if value:
            return value

    args_path = checkpoint_dir / "training_args.json"
    if args_path.exists():
        with open(args_path) as f:
            value = json.load(f).get("position")
        # train_sft.py defaults `position="last"` for ReFT, but for LoRA the
        # value is data-preprocessing-only (intervention_locations) and isn't
        # a vLLM-recognized lora_position — vLLM only accepts 'all' or 'prefill'.
        if value == "last":
            return "all"
        if value and value != "all":
            return value

    if (checkpoint_dir / "prefill_only_lora.json").exists():
        return "prefill"

    return None


def _load_lora_vllm(checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer, num_gpus, gpu_mem, enforce_eager):
    adapter_config_path = checkpoint_dir / "adapter_config.json"
    max_lora_rank = 16
    if adapter_config_path.exists():
        with open(adapter_config_path) as f:
            adapter_cfg = json.load(f)
        rank = adapter_cfg.get("r", adapter_cfg.get("lora_rank", 16))
        max_lora_rank = max(max_lora_rank, rank)

    tokenizer_source = resolve_tokenizer_source(checkpoint_dir, model_name)

    llm_kwargs = {
        "model": model_name,
        "tokenizer": str(tokenizer_source),
        "trust_remote_code": True,
        "enable_lora": True,
        "max_lora_rank": max_lora_rank,
        "tensor_parallel_size": max(1, num_gpus),
        "gpu_memory_utilization": gpu_mem,
    }
    if enforce_eager:
        llm_kwargs["enforce_eager"] = True

    llm = LLM(**llm_kwargs)

    # Prefill-only LoRA: forward lora_position through LoRARequest so vLLM
    # gates the LoRA delta to prompt tokens. Without this, decode also sees
    # the LoRA delta — a train/eval mismatch. Source of truth depends on
    # how the checkpoint was trained:
    #   * RL (eval_rl_full path):  training_config.json["lora_position"]
    #   * SFT prefill-only LoRA:   training_args.json["position"]
    #                              and/or marker prefill_only_lora.json
    lora_position = _detect_lora_position(checkpoint_dir)
    lora_kwargs = {}
    if lora_position:
        lora_kwargs["lora_position"] = lora_position
        print(f"  LoRA gating: lora_position={lora_position}")

    lora_request = LoRARequest("eval_adapter", 1, str(checkpoint_dir),
                               **lora_kwargs)
    return {"backend": "vllm", "llm": llm, "tokenizer": tokenizer, "lora_request": lora_request}

def _load_reft_hf(checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer, num_gpus):
    weights_path = _resolve_reft_weights_path(checkpoint_dir)
    if not weights_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"ReFT weights not found in {checkpoint_dir}")

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True,
        **{"device_map": "auto"} if num_gpus > 1 else {},
    )
    model = PreftModel.from_pretrained(model, checkpoint_dir)
    if num_gpus == 1:
        model = model.to("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model.eval()
    return {"backend": "hf", "model": model, "tokenizer": tokenizer}


def _load_lora_hf(checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer, num_gpus):
    from peft import PeftModel

    )
    model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, checkpoint_dir)
    if num_gpus == 1:
        model = model.to("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

    return {"backend": "hf", "model": model, "tokenizer": tokenizer}

    else:

        )

def load_checkpoint(checkpoint_dir, args):
    ckpt_type = _detect_checkpoint_type(checkpoint_dir)
    model_name = _get_base_model_name(checkpoint_dir)
    tokenizer = _load_tokenizer(checkpoint_dir, model_name)
    backend = args.backend

    # Decide backend
    use_vllm = backend != "hf"
    if use_vllm and not _HAS_VLLM:
        print("  vLLM not installed, falling back to HF backend.")
        use_vllm = False
    if use_vllm and ckpt_type == "reft" and not _HAS_VLLM_REFT:
        print("  vLLM ReFT fork not installed, falling back to HF backend.")
        use_vllm = False

    print(f"  Base model : {model_name}  ({args.num_gpus} GPU(s))  [{ckpt_type} + {'vllm' if use_vllm else 'hf'}]")

    if use_vllm:
        if ckpt_type == "reft":
            return _load_reft_vllm(
                checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer,
                args.num_gpus, args.gpu_memory_utilization, args.enforce_eager,
            )
        else:
            return _load_lora_vllm(
                checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer,
                args.num_gpus, args.gpu_memory_utilization, args.enforce_eager,
            )
    else:
        if ckpt_type == "reft":
            return _load_reft_hf(checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer, args.num_gpus)
        else:
            return _load_lora_hf(checkpoint_dir, model_name, tokenizer, args.num_gpus)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
#  Generation — vLLM                                                   #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

@torch.no_grad()
def _evaluate_vllm(llm, tokenizer, dataset, batch_size, max_new_tokens,
                   lora_request=None, num_samples_to_print=5,
                   dataset_name="gsm8k"):
    correct = 0
    total = 0
    printed = 0
    examples = []

    stop_ids = _collect_stop_ids(tokenizer)

    sampling_params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0.0,
        max_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        stop_token_ids=stop_ids,
    )

    for i in range(0, len(dataset), batch_size):
        batch = dataset[i : i + batch_size]
        prompts = batch["prompt"]
        ground_truths = batch["answer"]
        entry_points = batch.get("entry_point", [""] * len(prompts))

        outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params, lora_request=lora_request)
        completions = [o.outputs[0].text for o in outputs]

        for output, completion, ground_truth, prompt, ep in zip(
            outputs, completions, ground_truths, prompts, entry_points
        ):
            # For humaneval, score_humaneval needs the raw indented body —
            # extract_answer's strip() would break it.
            # humaneval, math, and gsm8k all pass the raw completion through:
            #  - humaneval: extract_answer's strip() destroys body indentation
            #  - math/gsm8k: math_verify (in check_answer_correct) does its
            #    own \boxed{} / expression extraction with LaTeX + numeric
            #    normalization, with a legacy fallback re-extracted from the
            #    raw completion.
            predicted = completion if dataset_name in ("humaneval", "math", "gsm8k") else extract_answer(completion, dataset_name)
            is_correct = check_answer_correct(predicted, ground_truth, dataset_name,
                                              entry_point=ep, prompt=prompt)
            if is_correct:
                correct += 1
            total += 1

            finish = getattr(output.outputs[0], "finish_reason", None)
            examples.append({
                "idx": total - 1,
                "correct": is_correct,
                "prompt": prompt.strip(),
                # For humaneval, leading indent of the body is load-bearing for
                # scoring (see code_exec.score_humaneval). Save raw so the
                # results can be rescored later if the scoring rules change.
                "completion": completion if dataset_name == "humaneval" else completion.strip(),
                "predicted": predicted,
                "ground_truth": ground_truth,
                "finish_reason": finish,
            })

            if printed < num_samples_to_print:
                print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                print(f"[Example {printed+1}] {'CORRECT' if is_correct else 'WRONG'}")
                print(f"--- Prompt ---\n{prompt.strip()}")
                print(f"--- Completion ---\n{completion.strip()}")
                print(f"--- Predicted: {predicted}  |  Ground truth: {ground_truth} ---")
                printed += 1

        if total % (batch_size * 20) == 0 or total == len(dataset):
            print(f"  [{total:4d}/{len(dataset)}]  acc: {correct/total:.3f}")

    acc = correct / total if total > 0 else 0.0
    return acc, examples

@torch.no_grad()
def _evaluate_hf(model, tokenizer, dataset, batch_size, max_new_tokens,
                 num_samples_to_print=5, dataset_name="gsm8k"):
    correct = 0
    total = 0
    printed = 0
    examples = []

    input_device = next(model.parameters()).device

    for i in range(0, len(dataset), batch_size):
        batch = dataset[i : i + batch_size]
        prompts = batch["prompt"]
        ground_truths = batch["answer"]
        entry_points = batch.get("entry_point", [""] * len(prompts))

        inputs = tokenizer(
            prompts, return_tensors="pt", padding=True,
            truncation=True, max_length=512,
        ).to(input_device)

        outputs = model.generate(
            **inputs,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            do_sample=False,
            pad_token_id=tokenizer.pad_token_id,
            eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        )

        prompt_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]
        gen_ids = outputs[:, prompt_len:]
        completions = tokenizer.batch_decode(gen_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)

        for completion, ground_truth, prompt, ep in zip(
            completions, ground_truths, prompts, entry_points
        ):
            # humaneval, math, and gsm8k all pass the raw completion through:
            #  - humaneval: extract_answer's strip() destroys body indentation
            #  - math/gsm8k: math_verify (in check_answer_correct) does its
            #    own \boxed{} / expression extraction with LaTeX + numeric
            #    normalization, with a legacy fallback re-extracted from the
            #    raw completion.
            predicted = completion if dataset_name in ("humaneval", "math", "gsm8k") else extract_answer(completion, dataset_name)
            is_correct = check_answer_correct(predicted, ground_truth, dataset_name,
                                              entry_point=ep, prompt=prompt)
            if is_correct:
                correct += 1
            total += 1

            examples.append({
                "idx": total - 1,
                "correct": is_correct,
                "prompt": prompt.strip(),
                "completion": completion if dataset_name == "humaneval" else completion.strip(),
                "predicted": predicted,
                "ground_truth": ground_truth,
            })

            if printed < num_samples_to_print:
                print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                print(f"[Example {printed+1}] {'CORRECT' if is_correct else 'WRONG'}")
                print(f"--- Prompt ---\n{prompt.strip()}")
                print(f"--- Completion ---\n{completion.strip()}")
                print(f"--- Predicted: {predicted}  |  Ground truth: {ground_truth} ---")
                printed += 1

        if total % (batch_size * 20) == 0 or total == len(dataset):
            print(f"  [{total:4d}/{len(dataset)}]  acc: {correct/total:.3f}")

    acc = correct / total if total > 0 else 0.0
    return acc, examples

def eval_one(checkpoint_dir, test_dataset, args):
    try:
        result = load_checkpoint(checkpoint_dir, args)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        print(f"  Skipping: {e}")
        return None, []

    tokenizer = result["tokenizer"]
    backend = result["backend"]

    if backend == "vllm":
        acc, examples = _evaluate_vllm(
            result["llm"], tokenizer, test_dataset,
            args.batch_size, args.max_new_tokens,
            lora_request=result.get("lora_request"),
            num_samples_to_print=args.num_samples_to_print,
            dataset_name=args.dataset,
        )
        del result["llm"]
    else:
        acc, examples = _evaluate_hf(
            result["model"], tokenizer, test_dataset,
            args.batch_size, args.max_new_tokens,
            num_samples_to_print=args.num_samples_to_print,
            dataset_name=args.dataset,
        )
        del result["model"]

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    return acc, examples


def _save_results(out_path, checkpoint_name, acc, examples, args,
                  training_type=None):
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report = {
        "checkpoint": checkpoint_name,
        "training_type": training_type or "unknown",
        "dataset": getattr(args, "dataset", "gsm8k"),
        "timestamp": datetime.datetime.now().isoformat(),
        "args": {"max_new_tokens": args.max_new_tokens, "batch_size": args.batch_size},
        "summary": {
            "accuracy": round(acc, 4),
            "accuracy_pct": round(acc * 100, 2),
            "correct": sum(e["correct"] for e in examples),
            "total": len(examples),
        },
        "examples": examples,
    }
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
    print(f"  Results saved to {out_path}")

"""Code-execution rewards via the human-eval library.

Both MBPP and HumanEval are routed through `human_eval.execution.check_correctness`,
which runs candidate code in a subprocess with `reliability_guard()` (disables
dangerous builtins, resets cwd) and a wall-clock timeout.

MBPP's `test_list` is a list of bare asserts, not a `check()` function, so we
wrap it into the schema check_correctness expects.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import textwrap

from rl_training._human_eval.execution import check_correctness


def _mbpp_problem(test_list: list[str] | str) -> dict:
    """Wrap MBPP asserts into the {prompt,test,entry_point} schema."""
    if isinstance(test_list, str):
        tests = test_list.splitlines()
    else:
        tests = list(test_list)
    body = textwrap.indent("\n".join(tests), "    ")
    test_src = f"def check(_):\n{body}\n    return True\n"
    return {
        "task_id": "mbpp",
        "prompt": "",
        "test": test_src,
        "entry_point": "_mbpp_check_target",
    }


def _humaneval_problem(test_src: str, entry_point: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "task_id": "humaneval",
        "prompt": "",
        "test": test_src,
        "entry_point": entry_point,
    }


def score_mbpp(candidate_code: str, test_list, timeout: float = 3.0) -> bool:
    problem = _mbpp_problem(test_list)
    # Provide a stub for the entry point so `check(entry_point)` resolves.
    completion = candidate_code + f"\n{problem['entry_point']} = None\n"
    result = check_correctness(problem, completion, timeout=timeout)
    return bool(result.get("passed", False))


def score_humaneval(candidate_code: str, test_src: str, entry_point: str,
                    timeout: float = 3.0) -> bool:
    problem = _humaneval_problem(test_src, entry_point)
    result = check_correctness(problem, candidate_code, timeout=timeout)
    return bool(result.get("passed", False))

"""IntervenableLayer — decoder-layer wrapper that hosts a ReFT adapter on the
block output (residual stream)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .adapters._registry import ADAPTER_REGISTRY, LoReFTAdapter


class IntervenableLayer(nn.Module):
    """Wraps a transformer decoder layer with a residual-stream adapter."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        original_layer,
        layer_idx,
        hidden_size,
        low_rank_dim=64,
        position="last",
        frozen=False,
        logging=False,
        mode="loreft",
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer = original_layer
        self.layer_idx = layer_idx

        ref_param = next(original_layer.parameters())

        adapter_cls = ADAPTER_REGISTRY.get(mode, LoReFTAdapter)
        self.adapter = adapter_cls(
            hidden_size,
            low_rank_dim=low_rank_dim,
            position=position,
            device=ref_param.device,
            dtype=ref_param.dtype,
            frozen=frozen,
            layer_idx=layer_idx,
            logging=logging,
        )

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        try:
            return super().__getattr__(name)
        except AttributeError:
            return getattr(self.layer, name)

    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs):
        outputs = self.layer(*args, **kwargs)
        hidden_states = outputs[0] if isinstance(outputs, tuple) else outputs

        intervention_locations = getattr(self, "_intervention_locations", None)
        hidden_states = self.adapter(hidden_states, intervention_locations=intervention_locations)

        return (hidden_states,) + outputs[1:] if isinstance(outputs, tuple) else hidden_states

class ReFTTrainerScoringMixin:
    """Fallback rescoring overrides for TRL builds without the ReFT hook seams."""

    def _get_per_token_logps_and_entropies(
        self,
        model,
        input_ids,
        attention_mask,
        logits_to_keep,
        batch_size=None,
        compute_entropy=False,
        pixel_values=None,
        image_grid_thw=None,
        num_images=None,
        pixel_attention_mask=None,
        image_sizes=None,
        token_type_ids=None,
        mm_token_type_ids=None,
        pixel_position_ids=None,
        image_position_ids=None,
        **extra_model_kwargs,
    ):
        """Compute log-probs while keeping ReFT intervention boundaries prompt-only."""
        batch_size = batch_size or input_ids.size(0)
        all_logps = []
        all_entropies = []
        is_reft_model = getattr(model, "_intervention_config", None) is not None

        for start in range(0, input_ids.size(0), batch_size):
            input_ids_batch = input_ids[start : start + batch_size]
            attention_mask_batch = attention_mask[start : start + batch_size]

            model_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids_batch, "attention_mask": attention_mask_batch}
            img_start = img_end = None
            if image_grid_thw is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                rows_per_image = image_grid_thw.prod(dim=-1)
                rows_per_sample = torch.split(rows_per_image, num_images)
                rows_per_sample = torch.stack([sample.sum() for sample in rows_per_sample])
                cum_rows = torch.cat([torch.tensor([0], device=rows_per_sample.device), rows_per_sample.cumsum(0)])
                row_start, row_end = cum_rows[start].item(), cum_rows[start + batch_size].item()
                model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[row_start:row_end]
                cum_imgs = torch.tensor([0] + num_images).cumsum(0)
                img_start, img_end = cum_imgs[start], cum_imgs[start + batch_size]
                model_inputs["image_grid_thw"] = image_grid_thw[img_start:img_end]
            elif pixel_values is not None:
                if num_images is not None:
                    num_images_list = num_images.tolist() if isinstance(num_images, torch.Tensor) else list(num_images)
                    cum_imgs = [0]
                    for count in num_images_list:
                        cum_imgs.append(cum_imgs[-1] + int(count))
                    img_start, img_end = cum_imgs[start], cum_imgs[start + batch_size]
                    model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[img_start:img_end]
                else:
                    model_inputs["pixel_values"] = pixel_values[start : start + batch_size]
            if pixel_attention_mask is not None:
                model_inputs["pixel_attention_mask"] = pixel_attention_mask[start : start + batch_size]
            if image_sizes is not None:
                model_inputs["image_sizes"] = image_sizes[start : start + batch_size]
            if token_type_ids is not None:
                model_inputs["token_type_ids"] = token_type_ids[start : start + batch_size]
            if mm_token_type_ids is not None:
                model_inputs["mm_token_type_ids"] = mm_token_type_ids[start : start + batch_size]
            if pixel_position_ids is not None:
                model_inputs["pixel_position_ids"] = pixel_position_ids[start : start + batch_size]
            if image_position_ids is not None:
                if img_start is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                    model_inputs["image_position_ids"] = image_position_ids[img_start:img_end]
                else:
                    model_inputs["image_position_ids"] = image_position_ids[start : start + batch_size]
            for key, value in extra_model_kwargs.items():
                if value is None:
                    continue
                if key == "image_position_ids" and img_start is not None and pixel_values is not None:
                    model_inputs[key] = value[img_start:img_end]
                else:
                    model_inputs[key] = value[start : start + batch_size]

            if "logits_to_keep" in self.model_kwarg_keys:
                model_inputs["logits_to_keep"] = logits_to_keep + 1

            prepare_inputs = getattr(self, "_prepare_model_inputs_for_logprob_computation", None)
            if callable(prepare_inputs):
                model_inputs = prepare_inputs(
                    model,
                    model_inputs,
                    attention_mask=attention_mask_batch,
                    logits_to_keep=logits_to_keep,
                )

            model_inputs["use_cache"] = False

            had_prompt_mask = hasattr(model, "_prompt_mask")
            prev_prompt_mask = getattr(model, "_prompt_mask", None) if had_prompt_mask else None
            try:
                if is_reft_model:
                    if logits_to_keep > 0:
                        model._prompt_mask = attention_mask_batch[:, :-logits_to_keep]
                    else:
                        model._prompt_mask = attention_mask_batch
                    self._maybe_print_hf_prompt_debug(attention_mask_batch, logits_to_keep)

                forward_model = getattr(self, "_forward_model_for_logprob_computation", None)
                if callable(forward_model):
                    logits = forward_model(
                        model,
                        model_inputs,
                        attention_mask=attention_mask_batch,
                        logits_to_keep=logits_to_keep,
                    )
                else:
                    logits = model(**model_inputs).logits
            finally:
                if is_reft_model:
                    if had_prompt_mask:
                        model._prompt_mask = prev_prompt_mask
                    elif hasattr(model, "_prompt_mask"):
                        delattr(model, "_prompt_mask")

            logits = logits[:, :-1, :]
            logits = logits[:, -logits_to_keep:, :]
            logits = logits / self.temperature
            completion_ids = input_ids_batch[:, -logits_to_keep:]
            logps = selective_log_softmax(logits, completion_ids)
            all_logps.append(logps)

            if compute_entropy:
                with torch.no_grad():
                    entropies = entropy_from_logits(logits)
                all_entropies.append(entropies)

        logps = torch.cat(all_logps, dim=0)
        entropies = torch.cat(all_entropies, dim=0) if compute_entropy else None
        return logps, entropies

    def _compute_loss(self, model, inputs):
        model._prompt_mask = inputs["prompt_mask"]
        return super()._compute_loss(model, inputs)

    def _generate_and_score_completions(self, inputs):
        output = super()._generate_and_score_completions(inputs)
        return self._post_generate_and_score_completions(output)

"""Dataset preparation helpers for RL training/eval."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re

from datasets import concatenate_datasets, load_dataset


def _extract_boxed(solution: str) -> str:
    """Extract the final \\boxed{...} answer from a MATH solution, handling nested braces."""
    idx = solution.rfind("\\boxed{")
    if idx < 0:
        return solution.strip()
    start = idx + len("\\boxed{")
    depth = 1
    i = start
    while i < len(solution) and depth > 0:
        if solution[i] == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif solution[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
        i += 1
    return solution[start:i - 1].strip() if depth == 0 else solution[start:].strip()


def prepare_dataset(dataset_name: str, tokenizer=None, split: str = "train",
                    max_samples: int = None, shuffle_seed: int = 42):
    """Prepare prompt-only datasets for GRPO training and eval.

    When `max_samples` is set (used for eval), the dataset is shuffled with
    `shuffle_seed` BEFORE slicing. This matters for MATH, whose test split
    is `concatenate_datasets(7 subjects)` in subject order — without the
    shuffle, taking the first 256 rows yields an all-algebra eval set.
    """
    _tok = tokenizer
    del tokenizer

    if dataset_name == "gsm8k":
        dataset = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split=split)
    elif dataset_name == "math":
        # EleutherAI/hendrycks_math has 7 subject configs (algebra, geometry, etc.).
        # Concatenate all subjects to match the original MATH dataset.
        subjects = [
            "algebra", "counting_and_probability", "geometry", "intermediate_algebra",
            "number_theory", "prealgebra", "precalculus",
        ]
        parts = [load_dataset("EleutherAI/hendrycks_math", s, split=split) for s in subjects]
        dataset = concatenate_datasets(parts)
    elif dataset_name == "tulu":
        # Stream to avoid downloading the full 940k mixture.
        # Use split slicing if max_samples is set.
        n = max_samples or 50000
        dataset = load_dataset("allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture", split=f"{split}[:{n}]")
    elif dataset_name == "mbpp":
        # Full config: 974 examples (374 train / 90 val / 500 test / 10 prompt).
        # Fields: text (NL description), test_list (3 asserts), code (gold), task_id.
        # For training (split="train") we concatenate ALL four splits to maximize
        # training data — held-out eval is HumanEval, not MBPP test (see
        # train_rl.py). Note: this means a later `eval.py --dataset mbpp` run
        # scores on data the model trained on; use HumanEval for clean numbers.
        if split == "train":
            mbpp_splits = ("train", "validation", "test", "prompt")
            parts = [
                load_dataset("google-research-datasets/mbpp", "full", split=s)
                for s in mbpp_splits
            ]
            dataset = concatenate_datasets(parts)
        else:
            dataset = load_dataset("google-research-datasets/mbpp", "full", split=split)
    elif dataset_name == "humaneval":
        # Eval-only: 164 problems, only the "test" split exists.
        # Fields: prompt (signature + docstring), test (full check fn), entry_point.
        dataset = load_dataset("openai/openai_humaneval", split="test")
    elif dataset_name == "mmlu":
        # 57-subject multiple choice. "all" config concatenates every subject.
        # ~14k test examples. Fields: question, choices (4), answer (int 0-3).
        dataset = load_dataset("cais/mmlu", "all", split=split)
    elif dataset_name == "mmlu_pro":
        # ~12k test examples, up to 10 options per question.
        # Fields: question, options (list), answer (letter A-J), category.
        dataset = load_dataset("TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro", split=split)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown dataset: {dataset_name}")

    def format_query(example):
        if dataset_name == "gsm8k":
            question = example["question"]
            answer = example["answer"]
            gt_answer = answer.split("####")[-1].strip() if "####" in answer else ""
            query_text = f"Question: {question}\n\nAnswer:"
        elif dataset_name == "tulu":
            # Extract user prompt from messages format
            messages = example["messages"]
            user_msgs = [m["content"] for m in messages if m["role"] == "user"]
            query_text = user_msgs[0] if user_msgs else ""
            gt_answer = ""  # No ground truth for general SFT mixture
        elif dataset_name == "mbpp":
            tests = example["test_list"]
            query_text = (
                f"You are an expert Python programmer. Write a function that satisfies "
                f"the description and passes the tests.\n\n"
                f"Description: {example['text']}\n\n"
                f"Tests:\n" + "\n".join(tests) + "\n\n[BEGIN]\n"
            )
            gt_answer = "\n".join(tests)  # ground truth = asserts to run
        elif dataset_name == "humaneval":
            query_text = example["prompt"]  # already a Python prompt
            # `test` defines a check(candidate) function; the reward runner
            # invokes check(entry_point), so don't pre-append it here.
            gt_answer = example["test"]
        elif dataset_name == "mmlu":
            letters = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]
            options_block = "\n".join(
                f"{l}. {c}" for l, c in zip(letters, example["choices"])
            )
            query_text = (
                f"Question: {example['question']}\n{options_block}\n\n"
                f"Answer with only the letter (A, B, C, or D).\n\nAnswer:"
            )
            gt_answer = letters[example["answer"]]
        elif dataset_name == "mmlu_pro":
            options = example["options"]
            letters = [chr(ord("A") + i) for i in range(len(options))]
            options_block = "\n".join(f"{l}. {o}" for l, o in zip(letters, options))
            # Mirror lm_eval's mmlu_pro `doc_to_text` (zero-shot CoT). Pairs
            # with the `answer is X` regex extractor in rewards.py — without
            # the CoT cue the model rarely emits that pattern.
            query_text = (
                f"Question:\n{example['question']}\n"
                f"Options:\n{options_block}\n"
                f"Answer: Let's think step by step."
            )
            gt_answer = example["answer"]  # already a letter
        else:
            problem = example["problem"]
            gt_answer = _extract_boxed(example.get("solution", ""))
            query_text = (
                f"Problem: {problem}\n\n"
                f"Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \\boxed{{}}.\n\n"
                f"Solution:"
            )

        return {
            "prompt": query_text,
            "answer": gt_answer,
            "_dataset": dataset_name,
            # Only humaneval needs this; carry it on every row so HF datasets
            # has a uniform schema across mixes/shuffles.
            "entry_point": example.get("entry_point", "") if dataset_name == "humaneval" else "",
        }

    dataset = dataset.map(format_query, desc=f"Formatting {split}")

    if max_samples:
        # Shuffle deterministically before truncating so the eval subset is
        # representative across subjects (esp. for MATH).
        dataset = dataset.shuffle(seed=shuffle_seed)
        dataset = dataset.select(range(min(max_samples, len(dataset))))

    return dataset

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional


@dataclass
class PreftConfig:
    """Configuration for ReFT adapters on a transformer model.

    Analogous to ``peft.LoraConfig``.  Fully serialisable to / from JSON.

    The ReFT adapter is mounted on the decoder block output (residual stream).
    LoRA wrappers on individual ``nn.Linear`` projections inside each target
    layer can additionally be enabled via ``use_lora``; the two mounts are
    mutually exclusive on a single config (pick one).
    """

    # Which layers to intervene on
    layer_indices: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)

    # Adapter hyperparameters
    adapter_type: str = "loreft"
    low_rank_dim: int = 64
    position: str = "last"

    # Mount points
    use_residual: bool = True

    # LoRA mount: wraps target nn.Linear modules with a position-gated low-rank
    # update.  Independent of the ReFT mount above; cannot be combined.
    use_lora: bool = False
    lora_target_modules: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    lora_alpha: float = 16.0
    lora_dropout: float = 0.0
    lora_rank: Optional[int] = None  # falls back to low_rank_dim if None

    # Frozen adapters (no gradient)
    frozen: bool = False
    logging: bool = False

    # Auto-populated from model
    hidden_size: Optional[int] = None

    # Metadata
    base_model_name_or_path: Optional[str] = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        if isinstance(self.layer_indices, int):
            self.layer_indices = [self.layer_indices]
        if self.use_lora and not self.lora_target_modules:
            raise ValueError(
                "use_lora=True requires lora_target_modules "
                "(e.g. ['q_proj', 'v_proj'])"
            )
        if self.use_lora and self.use_residual:
            raise ValueError(
                "Mixed ReFT + LoRA mounts are currently not supported in a single "
                "PreftConfig.  Pick one:\n"
                "  - ReFT only: set use_lora=False (keep use_residual)\n "
                "  - LoRA only: set use_residual=False and leave use_lora=True."
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    #  Serialisation                                                       #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)

    def save_pretrained(self, save_directory: str | Path):
        path = Path(save_directory)
        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(path / "preft_config.json", "w") as f:
            json.dump(self.to_dict(), f, indent=2)

    def save(self, path: str | Path):
        """Backward-compatible save to a single JSON file."""
        path = Path(path)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(self.to_dict(), f, indent=2)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> PreftConfig:
        """Backward-compatible load from a single JSON file."""
        with open(path) as f:
            return cls.from_dict(json.load(f))

    @classmethod
    def from_pretrained(cls, path: str | Path) -> PreftConfig:
        """Load from a local directory or a single JSON file.

        Accepts the current ``preft_config.json`` filename and the legacy
        ``reft_config.json`` / ``intervention_config.json`` names so that
        checkpoints written by older versions still load.
        """
        path = Path(path)
        if path.is_dir():
            for fname in ("preft_config.json", "reft_config.json", "intervention_config.json"):
                candidate = path / fname
                if candidate.exists():
                    config_file = candidate
                    break
            else:
                config_file = path / "preft_config.json"
        else:
            config_file = path
        with open(config_file) as f:
            return cls.from_dict(json.load(f))

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> PreftConfig:
        """Construct from dict, accepting aliases for backward compat."""
        aliases = {
            "rank": "low_rank_dim",
            "reft_rank": "low_rank_dim",
            "layers": "layer_indices",
            "reft_layers": "layer_indices",
            "layer_idx": "layer_indices",
            "mode": "adapter_type",
        }
        normalized = {aliases.get(k, k): v for k, v in d.items()}
        valid = {f.name for f in fields(cls)}
        return cls(**{k: v for k, v in normalized.items() if k in valid})

"""Monkey-patches that add preft's required hooks to upstream TRL.

When this module is imported it patches:
  trl.generation.vllm_generation.VLLMGeneration.__init__   — adds extra_llm_kwargs,
      auto-injects enable_lora for preft LoRA-only models, brackets LLM() with
      vllm.reft.set_reft_spec/clear_reft_spec for preft ReFT models.
  VLLMGeneration._fix_param_name_to_vllm  — ReFT name remapping (.layer. / .adapter.)
  VLLMGeneration.sync_weights             — ReFT collective_rpc path + buffer sync
                                            + refresh_reft_caches, plus LoRA-only
                                            sync_lora_weights + pin LoRARequest.
  VLLMGeneration.generate                 — threads _lora_request into llm.generate().

Together this lets preft RL training run against upstream TRL on PyPI; the
custom fork at github.com/lanpouthakoun/trl is no longer required.

Apply happens exactly once.  Re-importing is a no-op.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import functools
import logging
import re

import torch
from torch import nn

logger = logging.getLogger("preft._trl_patches")

_PATCHED_ATTR = "_preft_patched"


def _detect_preft_model(model: nn.Module):
    """Return (unwrapped_model, intervention_config) or (unwrapped, None)."""
    inner = getattr(model, "module", model)
    cfg = getattr(inner, "_intervention_config", None)
    if cfg is None:
        cfg = getattr(inner, "preft_config", None)
    return inner, cfg


def _is_reft_mount(cfg) -> bool:
    return bool(cfg is not None and getattr(cfg, "use_residual", False))


def _is_lora_only_mount(cfg) -> bool:
    return bool(
        cfg is not None
        and getattr(cfg, "use_lora", False)
        and not getattr(cfg, "use_residual", False)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patched VLLMGeneration.__init__
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _make_patched_init(orig_init):
    @functools.wraps(orig_init)
    def patched_init(self, *args, extra_llm_kwargs: dict | None = None, **kwargs):
        # Stash for reference inside other methods.
        self.extra_llm_kwargs = dict(extra_llm_kwargs or {})
        self._lora_request = None

        # Resolve the model arg (positional 0 or kwarg).
        model = kwargs.get("model")
        if model is None and args:
            model = args[0]
        inner, cfg = _detect_preft_model(model) if model is not None else (None, None)

        # For preft LoRA-only models, auto-enable_lora on the vLLM LLM() ctor.
        if _is_lora_only_mount(cfg):
            rank = cfg.lora_rank if cfg.lora_rank is not None else cfg.low_rank_dim
            self.extra_llm_kwargs.setdefault("enable_lora", True)
            self.extra_llm_kwargs.setdefault("max_lora_rank", max(8, int(rank)))
            self.extra_llm_kwargs.setdefault("max_loras", 1)
            logger.info(
                "preft: auto-enabled LoRA on vLLM (rank=%d, target_modules=%s)",
                rank, list(cfg.lora_target_modules),
            )

        # For preft ReFT models, bracket the upstream __init__ with reft_spec
        # injection so vLLM's LLM() ctor sees the spec on VllmConfig.
        reft_active = _is_reft_mount(cfg)
        spec_mgr = None
        if reft_active:
            try:
                import vllm.reft as _vllm_reft
                from preft.utils import export_vllm_reft_spec
                spec = export_vllm_reft_spec(inner)
                _vllm_reft.set_reft_spec(spec)
                spec_mgr = _vllm_reft
                logger.info("preft: injected ReFT spec for %d layer(s) into vLLM",
                            len(spec["layer_indices"]))
            except ImportError:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "preft ReFT model with use_vllm=True requires the vllm fork "
                    "exposing vllm.reft (set_reft_spec/clear_reft_spec/sync_reft_weights). "
                    "Install the forked vllm or disable use_vllm for ReFT modes."
                )

        try:
            orig_init(self, *args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            if spec_mgr is not None:
                try:
                    spec_mgr.clear_reft_spec()
                except Exception:
                    pass

    return patched_init


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patched VLLMGeneration._fix_param_name_to_vllm (ReFT-aware name remap)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _make_patched_fix_param_name(orig_fn):
    _layer_prefix_re_adapter = re.compile(r"(layers\.\d+)\.adapter\.")
    _layer_prefix_re_qkv = re.compile(r"(layers\.\d+)\.layer\.self_attn\.attn\.")
    _layer_prefix_re_base = re.compile(r"(layers\.\d+)\.layer\.")

    @functools.wraps(orig_fn)
    def patched(self, name: str, extra_prefixes=None):
        # Strip the peft/preft outer wrapper prefix before the upstream cleanup.
        extra_prefixes = list(extra_prefixes or [])
        if "base_model." not in extra_prefixes:
            extra_prefixes.append("base_model.")

        # Upstream returns just the inner-stripped name; we then apply ReFT remap
        # if we detect an intervention config on the model.
        cleaned = orig_fn(self, name, extra_prefixes=extra_prefixes)

        _, cfg = _detect_preft_model(self.model)
        if cfg is not None:
            cleaned = _layer_prefix_re_adapter.sub(r"\1.reft_adapter.", cleaned)
            cleaned = _layer_prefix_re_qkv.sub(r"\1.self_attn.", cleaned)
            cleaned = _layer_prefix_re_base.sub(r"\1.", cleaned)
        return cleaned

    return patched


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patched VLLMGeneration.sync_weights (ReFT + LoRA-only fast paths)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _make_patched_sync_weights(orig_sync):
    @functools.wraps(orig_sync)
    def patched_sync(self):
        inner, cfg = _detect_preft_model(self.model)

        # ---- LoRA-only path: push the adapter state dict via sync_lora_weights.
        if _is_lora_only_mount(cfg) and self.mode == "colocate":
            state_dict, peft_config_dict = inner.lora_state_dict_for_vllm()
            lora_int_id = 1
            if hasattr(self.llm, "collective_rpc"):
                self.llm.collective_rpc(
                    "sync_lora_weights",
                    args=(state_dict, peft_config_dict, lora_int_id),
                )
                # Pin a LoRARequest so subsequent generate() calls apply the
                # adapter at the configured position (typically "prefill").
                if self._lora_request is None:
                    try:
                        from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest
                        self._lora_request = LoRARequest(
                            lora_name="preft_lora",
                            lora_int_id=lora_int_id,
                            lora_path="/unused",
                            lora_position=getattr(cfg, "position", "prefill"),
                        )
                    except TypeError:
                        # Upstream LoRARequest doesn't have lora_position; fall
                        # back to without it.
                        from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest
                        self._lora_request = LoRARequest(
                            lora_name="preft_lora",
                            lora_int_id=lora_int_id,
                            lora_path="/unused",
                        )
                self.llm.reset_prefix_cache()
                logger.info("preft: synced LoRA adapter (%d tensors)", len(state_dict))
                return

        # ---- ReFT colocate fast path: collective_rpc("sync_reft_weights").
        if _is_reft_mount(cfg) and self.mode == "colocate" and not self.is_fsdp_enabled:
            weight_dict: dict[int, dict[str, torch.Tensor]] = {}
            for idx, layer in enumerate(inner.model.layers):
                adapter = getattr(layer, "adapter", None)
                if adapter is None:
                    continue
                weight_dict[idx] = {
                    k: v.data.contiguous() for k, v in adapter.state_dict().items()
                }
            if weight_dict and hasattr(self.llm, "collective_rpc"):
                self.llm.collective_rpc("sync_reft_weights", args=(weight_dict, False))
                self.llm.collective_rpc("refresh_reft_caches")
                self.llm.reset_prefix_cache()
                logger.info("preft: synced ReFT adapters for %d layer(s)", len(weight_dict))
                return

        # ---- Fallback: upstream sync_weights (handles peft, FSDP, deepspeed).
        orig_sync(self)

        # In server mode (no collective_rpc fast path), buffer-sync + refresh.
        if self.mode == "server" and self.accelerator.is_main_process and _is_reft_mount(cfg):
            for name, buf in inner.named_buffers():
                if "parametrizations." not in name:
                    continue
                vllm_name = self._fix_param_name_to_vllm(name)
                if vllm_name is None:
                    continue
                self.vllm_client.update_named_param(vllm_name, buf.data.contiguous())
            self.vllm_client.refresh_reft_caches()

    return patched_sync


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patched VLLMGeneration.generate (thread _lora_request through llm.generate)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _make_patched_generate(orig_generate):
    @functools.wraps(orig_generate)
    def patched_generate(self, *args, **kwargs):
        lora_request = getattr(self, "_lora_request", None)
        if lora_request is None:
            return orig_generate(self, *args, **kwargs)

        # Inject lora_request into llm.generate() / vllm_client.generate() calls
        # made inside orig_generate by monkey-patching them on the instance for
        # the duration of this call.
        if self.mode == "colocate":
            llm = self.llm
            orig_llm_generate = llm.generate

            @functools.wraps(orig_llm_generate)
            def llm_generate_with_lora(*a, **kw):
                kw.setdefault("lora_request", lora_request)
                return orig_llm_generate(*a, **kw)

            llm.generate = llm_generate_with_lora
            try:
                return orig_generate(self, *args, **kwargs)
            finally:
                llm.generate = orig_llm_generate
        else:
            client = self.vllm_client
            orig_client_generate = client.generate

            @functools.wraps(orig_client_generate)
            def client_generate_with_lora(*a, **kw):
                kw.setdefault("lora_request", lora_request)
                return orig_client_generate(*a, **kw)

            client.generate = client_generate_with_lora
            try:
                return orig_generate(self, *args, **kwargs)
            finally:
                client.generate = orig_client_generate

    return patched_generate


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional GRPOTrainer no-op hooks (for legacy mixin code that calls super())
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _install_default_hooks(GRPOTrainer):
    """Add no-op default implementations of the fork's hooks if not present.

    These let any preft mixin that overrides them and calls ``super().hook()``
    work cleanly even though upstream TRL never invokes the hooks itself.
    The hooks are still effectively dead in upstream — we eliminate the need
    for them by handling the ReFT/LoRA logic inside VLLMGeneration directly.
    """
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "on_before_vllm_generation_init"):
        GRPOTrainer.on_before_vllm_generation_init = lambda self: None
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "on_after_vllm_generation_init"):
        GRPOTrainer.on_after_vllm_generation_init = lambda self: None
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "get_extra_vllm_kwargs"):
        GRPOTrainer.get_extra_vllm_kwargs = lambda self: {}
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "sync_model_to_generation_backend"):
        GRPOTrainer.sync_model_to_generation_backend = (
            lambda self: self.vllm_generation.sync_weights()
        )
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "_post_generate_and_score_completions"):
        GRPOTrainer._post_generate_and_score_completions = lambda self, output: output
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "_prepare_model_inputs_for_logprob_computation"):
        def _prep(self, model, model_inputs, *, attention_mask, logits_to_keep):
            return model_inputs
        GRPOTrainer._prepare_model_inputs_for_logprob_computation = _prep
    if not hasattr(GRPOTrainer, "_forward_model_for_logprob_computation"):
        def _fwd(self, model, model_inputs, *, attention_mask, logits_to_keep):
            return model(**model_inputs).logits
        GRPOTrainer._forward_model_for_logprob_computation = _fwd


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Log filter: vLLM's `non-default args` INFO line includes the entire
# reft_config blueprint, which embeds serialized tensor bytes — pages of
# unreadable hex.  Replace bytes literals with <bytes elided> so the log
# stays useful without losing visibility of the other non-default args.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_BYTES_LITERAL_RE = None
_LOG_FILTER_INSTALLED = False


def _install_log_filter():
    global _BYTES_LITERAL_RE, _LOG_FILTER_INSTALLED
    if _LOG_FILTER_INSTALLED:
        return
    import logging as _logging
    import re as _re

    # Match a Python bytes literal: b'...' where the body is any combination
    # of \xHH escapes, other backslash escapes, or non-quote chars.
    _BYTES_LITERAL_RE = _re.compile(
        r"b'(?:\\x[0-9a-fA-F]{2}|\\.|[^'\\])*'", _re.DOTALL
    )

    class _ReftBlobFilter(_logging.Filter):
        def filter(self, record):
            try:
                msg = record.getMessage()
            except Exception:
                return True
            if "reft_config" in msg and "b'" in msg:
                record.msg = _BYTES_LITERAL_RE.sub("<bytes elided>", msg)
                record.args = ()
            return True

    filt = _ReftBlobFilter()
    for name in ("vllm", "vllm.utils", "vllm.engine", "vllm.engine.arg_utils"):
        _logging.getLogger(name).addFilter(filt)
    _LOG_FILTER_INSTALLED = True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def apply_patches() -> bool:
    """Install all patches. Returns True if applied, False if already patched
    or trl is not available."""
    try:
        from trl.generation import vllm_generation as _vg
        from trl.trainer import GRPOTrainer
    except ImportError:
        logger.debug("trl not installed; preft TRL patches not applied")
        return False

    VLLMGen = _vg.VLLMGeneration
    if getattr(VLLMGen, _PATCHED_ATTR, False):
        return False

    VLLMGen.__init__ = _make_patched_init(VLLMGen.__init__)
    VLLMGen._fix_param_name_to_vllm = _make_patched_fix_param_name(
        VLLMGen._fix_param_name_to_vllm
    )
    VLLMGen.sync_weights = _make_patched_sync_weights(VLLMGen.sync_weights)
    VLLMGen.generate = _make_patched_generate(VLLMGen.generate)

    _install_default_hooks(GRPOTrainer)
    _install_log_filter()

    setattr(VLLMGen, _PATCHED_ATTR, True)
    logger.info("preft: TRL patches applied (VLLMGeneration + GRPOTrainer defaults + log filter)")
    return True

    gradient_checkpointing: bool = False
    use_flash_attn: bool = False

def resolve_reft_layers(mode: str, reft_layers, model_name: str) -> Optional[list[int]]:
    """Resolve adapter layer selection from CLI/YAML-friendly inputs."""
    if mode not in ADAPTER_REGISTRY:
        return None
    if isinstance(reft_layers, list):
        return [int(layer_idx) for layer_idx in reft_layers]
    if reft_layers == "all":
        model_config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_name)
        return list(range(model_config.num_hidden_layers))
    return [int(layer_idx) for layer_idx in str(reft_layers).split(",")]


def build_run_name(config: ExperimentConfig) -> str:
    """Build the default wandb/output run name."""
    model_short = config.model_name.split("/")[-1]
    world_size = int(os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", "1"))
    eff_bs = config.batch_size * config.gradient_accumulation_steps * world_size
    if config.mode == "full_finetune":
        return f"{model_short}_{config.dataset}_grpo_fullft_lr{config.learning_rate:.0e}"
    if config.mode == "lora":
        pos_suffix = f"_pos{config.lora_position}" if config.lora_position != "all" else ""
        # Only encode alpha when explicitly set; sweeps that rely on the default
        # (alpha=32 in train_rl.py) keep their existing dir names unchanged.
        alpha_suffix = f"_alpha{config.lora_alpha}" if config.lora_alpha is not None else ""
        backend_suffix = "_preft" if config.lora_backend == "preft" else ""
        return (
            f"{model_short}_{config.dataset}_grpo_lora"
            f"_r{config.lora_rank}_lr{config.learning_rate:.0e}"
            f"{pos_suffix}{alpha_suffix}{backend_suffix}"
        )
    if config.mode in ADAPTER_REGISTRY:
        # Include position in the name so prefill and all-position sweeps with
        # otherwise identical hyperparams don't collide on disk.
        pos = config.reft_position or "last"
        return (
            f"{model_short}_{config.dataset}_grpo_{config.mode}"
            f"_r{config.reft_rank}_lr{config.learning_rate:.0e}_pos{pos}"
            f"_bs{eff_bs}"
        )
    return f"{model_short}_{config.dataset}_{config.mode}_lr{config.learning_rate:.0e}"


def build_experiment_config(args, learning_rate: Optional[float] = None) -> ExperimentConfig:
    """Construct an ExperimentConfig from argparse args."""
    lora_modules = args.lora_modules
    if isinstance(lora_modules, str):

class DistillationTrainerMixin:
    """On-policy distillation: load teacher adapter as the GRPO reference model.

    GRPO's existing KL penalty (beta * KL(policy || ref)) does all the work.
    We just load the teacher checkpoint as the "ref" adapter instead of
    the initial policy weights.
    """

    def _is_distillation(self) -> bool:
        return getattr(self.args, "teacher_adapter_path", None) is not None

    def on_after_vllm_generation_init(self):
        super().on_after_vllm_generation_init()
        if not self._is_distillation():
            return
        model = self.accelerator.unwrap_model(self.model)
        teacher_path = self.args.teacher_adapter_path
        print(f"[Distillation] Loading teacher as 'ref' adapter from {teacher_path}")
        # Replace the "ref" adapter (GRPO's frozen reference) with the teacher
        if "ref" in model.peft_config:
            model.delete_adapter("ref")
        model.load_adapter(teacher_path, adapter_name="ref")
        # Freeze teacher/ref weights
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if ".ref." in name:
                param.requires_grad = False
        model.set_adapter("default")
        print(f"[Distillation] Adapters: {list(model.peft_config.keys())}")
